analysis: The trial executed successfully but achieved macro validation HR@10 of 0.4912, below the recorded best of 0.5400 by 0.0488. Category HR@10 was 0.5400 for Movies_and_TV, 0.5100 for Industrial_and_Scientific, 0.4300 for Electronics, and 0.4850 for CDs_and_Vinyl. Direct item-embedding attention did not improve the recorded best. Without matched recurrent-memory results, the decline cannot be attributed conclusively to this change alone. Electronics had the lowest category score. No test results were accessed or reported.
code_summary: One independently trained network and one selected checkpoint per category, with dataset routing preserved. A two-layer, 128-dimensional GRU supplies queries to causal attention whose keys and values come directly from jointly learned item embeddings. A sigmoid gate adds the projected attention context to recurrent states, followed by LayerNorm, dropout, and an output projection. Candidates use tied item embeddings plus learned item biases. Training uses BPR-max with 1,024 shared sampled negatives, observed-item masking, AdamW, and validation-based checkpoint selection. The predictor writer embeds the same architecture and loads exactly one checkpoint per category; no ensemble or separately fitted scoring component is used.
